common.update_summary_older: The receiver runs an older plugin than this integration carries. Installing replaces it with the bundled {version} and leaves the receiver's own broker settings alone.
common.update_summary_older_no_install: The receiver runs an older plugin than the bundled {version}. No SSH credentials are stored, so this card cannot install it: reconfigure the receiver with “Keep SSH credentials for updates”, or install the IPK on the box by hand.
common.update_summary_newer: The receiver runs a plugin newer than the bundled {version}. Nothing here replaces it — this card never offers a downgrade.

menu_options.manual: Use an existing MQTT Bridge plugin

confirm.title: Add this Enigma2 receiver
confirm.description:
Enigma2 box {name} ({boxtype}, {image}) has announced itself on the broker.

Adding it switches the box into integration mode: the plugin withdraws the MQTT discovery entities it publishes on its own, and Home Assistant builds the device instead. The box has to confirm the switch before it is added.

manual.title: Add an Enigma2 receiver by hand
manual.description: Use this when the receiver's announcement never reached Home Assistant, for example because the box publishes through an MQTT bridge that rewrites the topic prefix.

data_description.base_topic: The prefix the receiver publishes under, as Home Assistant sees it on the broker. The plugin's default is `enigma2`.
data_description.node_id: The receiver's node ID, shown on the plugin's setup screen. It is the box type and the last six digits of the MAC address, for example `vuuno4kse_005301`.
data_description.name: What to call this receiver in Home Assistant. Left empty, the name the plugin reports is used.
data_description.receiver_host: Hostname or IP address used only for the device link and as a suggestion when configuring SSH. MQTT-only setups may leave it empty.

install.title: Connect to the receiver
install.description: Home Assistant reads the SSH host key before asking for a password.

install_confirm.title: Confirm receiver identity and install
install_confirm.description:
Confirm SSH fingerprint `{fingerprint}` before sending credentials. The plugin is installed from the bundle shipped with this integration.

**Give the receiver a broker login of its own.** The receiver keeps that password in a file on its own flash, and most Enigma2 images answer SSH with the image's default root password — so a login shared with Home Assistant hands over the whole broker.

On a standalone Mosquitto these four lines confine the login to one receiver — put its own node ID where the example stands:

- `topic readwrite enigma2/vuuno4kse_005301/#`
- `topic write enigma2mqtt/discovery/vuuno4kse_005301/#`
- `topic write homeassistant/device/vuuno4kse_005301/#`
- `topic write homeassistant/device_automation/vuuno4kse_005301/#`

The Home Assistant Mosquitto add-on does **not** enforce an `acl_file` today: it accepts the file and never asks it. There a dedicated login names the receiver in the broker log but does not confine it, so treat the receiver as able to publish anywhere until the add-on gains ACL support.

data_description.broker_host: The broker address as the receiver reaches it. The receiver is the one that connects, so this has to work from the receiver's network — Home Assistant's own broker setting is not necessarily the same address.
data_description.broker_port: The broker's MQTT port. 1883 unless the broker was moved.
data_description.broker_username: The login created for this receiver alone. Do not reuse the one Home Assistant connects with.
data_description.broker_password: Written to the receiver in a file only root can read. It never reaches a Home Assistant log or the diagnostics download.

reauth_confirm_host_key.title: SSH host key changed
reauth_confirm_host_key.description: Only continue if the receiver now shows fingerprint `{fingerprint}`.

reconfigure.title: Change where this receiver publishes
reconfigure.description:
Use this after changing the node ID or the base topic on the receiver's own setup screen.

Changing the node ID changes the receiver's identity: its entities are rebuilt with new IDs and their history stays with the old device, which is removed. Changing only the base topic or the name keeps everything.

data_description.base_topic: The prefix the receiver publishes under, as Home Assistant sees it on the broker.
data_description.node_id: The receiver's node ID, shown on the plugin's setup screen.
data_description.name: What to call this receiver in Home Assistant.
data_description.receiver_host: Changing this metadata does not replace pinned SSH credentials; re-enrol SSH separately when the receiver changes.

init.title: Receiver options
init.description: The receiver reports the MAC address {mac}. Magic packets go there unless another one is given below.

data.dangerous_buttons: Show the deep standby and reboot buttons
data.configure_ssh: Configure SSH credentials for plugin updates
data.source_list_scope: Channels in the media player's source list

data_description.dangerous_buttons: Deep standby takes the receiver off the network until a magic packet wakes it, and reboot interrupts whatever it is doing. Two gates have to be open before the buttons appear: this option, and the receiver's own permission for deep standby, which is set on the box itself under Menu → Plugins → MQTT Bridge and cannot be changed from here. An older plugin that does not report that permission leaves this option deciding alone. The buttons are hidden by default so that neither is one mis-tap away on a shared dashboard, and the plugin refuses both while a recording is running, whatever is set here.
data_description.wol_mac: Leave empty to use the address the receiver reports. Set it when the receiver reports a different interface from the one that is plugged in — a box on Wi-Fi does not answer a magic packet sent to its cable port.
data_description.bouquets: Which bouquets the channel list and the media browser offer. Leave empty for every bouquet the receiver publishes.
data_description.publish_keys: Remote key events can drive automations, but they also reveal what is pressed. Turn this off when no automation needs them.
data_description.screenshot: Off publishes no new screen images. On zap captures after a channel change. Interval captures repeatedly at the interval below.
data_description.screenshot_interval: Used only in interval mode. The receiver enforces a minimum of five seconds.
data_description.screenshot_delay: Wait before an automatic screenshot after a channel change, so the new picture has time to appear.
data_description.cam_telemetry: Expose the current service's encryption and ECM status. No server, account or card details are published.
data_description.oscam_telemetry: Expose privacy-neutral OSCam process, API, reader and server health. Reader labels, addresses, accounts and card identifiers are never published.
data_description.check_github_releases: Off by default, and off means this integration talks to nothing but your broker. On, it asks the plugin's repository which release is published, at most once every 24 hours, and says so on the version entity. The answer and the time it was asked are saved, so reloading the receiver or restarting Home Assistant shows what is already known rather than asking again. It never downloads anything: installing still uses only the bundle shipped here.
data_description.source_list_scope: Every bouquet on offer is one list of all of them, which is what this integration has always done — on a receiver with a thousand channels that is a dropdown of a thousand rows. The active bouquet is the short list the receiver itself is on, the one its channel up and down walk, and the same one the “Channel” select shows; a receiver that has published no active bouquet keeps the long list, because there is nothing to shorten it to. Either way the “Bouquet” select changes bouquets, and the zap action takes a service reference and ignores this setting.

ssh_confirm.title: Confirm SSH identity
ssh_confirm.description: Confirm receiver fingerprint `{fingerprint}` before sending credentials.

error.plugin_unavailable: The receiver is not connected, so its privacy settings were not changed. Try again when it is online.
error.plugin_config_failed: The receiver did not confirm the new privacy settings. Its previous settings and these Home Assistant options were kept.
error.invalid_mac: That is not a MAC address. Write it as `00:00:5e:00:53:01`, `00-00-5e-00-53-01`, `0000.5e00.5301` or `00005e005301`, or leave the field empty to use the address the receiver reports.

zap.name: Zap
zap.description: Tunes the receiver to a channel, by service reference or by name. Give exactly one of the two.

sref.name: Service reference
sref.description: The channel's service reference, trailing colon included. This is the identifier that never changes.

name.name: Channel name
name.description: The channel's name as the bouquet spells it. Refused by the receiver when more than one channel in its configured bouquets has that name.

select_bouquet.name: Select bouquet
select_bouquet.description: Makes a bouquet the receiver's active channel list. Channel up and down then follow that bouquet.

sref.name: Bouquet reference
sref.description: The service reference of a bouquet published by the receiver. If the current channel is outside it, the receiver tunes its first playable channel.

send_key.name: Send key
send_key.description: Injects a remote control key into the receiver, as if somebody had pressed it.

key.name: Key
key.description: The key name, such as `KEY_RED`. `red` works too.

long.name: Long press
long.description: Send it as a held button rather than a tap.

message.name: Show message
message.description: Puts a popup on the television. The receiver cuts the text at 500 characters.

type.name: Type
type.description: Which icon and colour the popup uses.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: How long the popup stays on screen, in seconds.

add_timer.name: Add timer
add_timer.description: Adds a recording timer, either from an EPG event or from a start and end time. Give the event ID, or both times — not both forms.

event_id.name: Event ID
event_id.description: The EPG event to record. Prefer this: the receiver resolves the event itself, so the timer gets the programme's name and the padding the box is set up with.

begin.name: Start
begin.description: When to start recording, for a manual window.

end.name: End
end.description: When to stop recording, for a manual window.

name.name: Name
name.description: What to call the recording, for a manual window.

delete_timer.name: Delete timer
delete_timer.description: Deletes a recording timer. enigma2 identifies a timer by its channel, start and end, so all three are needed.

record.name: Record
record.description: Starts or stops an instant recording of whatever is on.

screenshot.name: Take a screenshot
screenshot.description: Captures what is on the television now and publishes it, which is what refreshes the Screen image entity.

set_ha_mode.name: Set Home Assistant mode
set_ha_mode.description: Switches how the receiver presents itself: through this integration, through MQTT discovery, or not at all. Switching away from integration mode leaves this integration's entities without anything updating them.

mode.name: Mode
mode.description: Which mode the plugin should run in.

get_epg_grid.name: Get the EPG grid
get_epg_grid.description: Returns what is on, per bouquet, as the receiver last published it. Use it in a template or a script; it is deliberately not an entity attribute, because a grid is tens of kilobytes per bouquet and would be written to the recorder database on every refresh.

bouquet.name: Bouquet
bouquet.description: One bouquet, by name or by slug. Left empty, every published bouquet is returned.

mqtt_not_available.message: The MQTT integration is not available, so the receiver cannot be reached.

command_timeout.message: The receiver did not carry out `{command}`. Check that it is on and that the plugin is running.

zap_needs_one.message: Give either a service reference or a channel name, not both and not neither.

timer_needs_event_or_window.message: A timer needs either an event ID or both a start and an end time.

timer_takes_one_form.message: Give an event ID or a start and end time, not both.

unknown_bouquet.message: The receiver has published no EPG grid for the bouquet {bouquet}.

bouquet_not_published.message: The receiver does not offer the bouquet {bouquet}.

bouquet_context_unsupported.message: This receiver plugin cannot activate a bouquet context. Update the plugin to use this action.

unknown_channel.message: No channel called {channel} is in the bouquets this receiver offers.

unsupported_media_type.message: A receiver can play a channel, not {media_type}.

wake_on_lan_unavailable.message: The Wake on LAN integration is not set up, so no magic packet can be sent. Add it from Settings, then try again.

no_mac.message: This receiver has not reported a MAC address, so there is nowhere to send a magic packet. Set one in the integration's options.

update_version_unknown.message: The receiver has not reported its installed plugin version.

update_downgrade.message: Refusing to replace a newer plugin with an older bundled version.

update_version_unavailable.message: The requested version is not available from this integration’s verified bundle.

update_no_credentials.message: No SSH credentials are stored for this receiver. Reconfigure it and tick “Keep SSH credentials for updates”, then try again.

channel_not_in_active_bouquet.message: {channel} is not in the bouquet the receiver is on, so the source list does not offer it. Switch the “Bouquet” select to the bouquet it belongs to first, or use the enigma2_mqtt.zap action, which takes a service reference and is not scoped.

option_no_longer_offered.message: {option} is no longer on this list. The receiver republished its channels while it was being chosen; open the list again and pick from what is there now.
